findings.claim: The span's bytes are one syntactically continuous sentence rather than atomic sayings cohering, so proverb_cluster mis-types the unit the row itself describes.
findings.grounds: Byte tier, every run spliced from the staged verse map: 6:12 carries the run's only nominal subject, אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן , and its first participial predicate, ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה ; 6:13 is entirely dependent - קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו - three participial forms with prepositional phrases, carrying no subject noun and no prefix- or suffix-conjugation verb of its own, and 6:14 continues under the same third-person masculine singular reference, תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ , before the apodosis opens at 6:15 with עַל כֵּ֗ן . The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the form reading is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings: WEB renders 6:13 as bare relative clauses depending on 6:12, “who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,” (web:Prov.6.13). A proverb_cluster row claims that atomic sayings cohere as one unit; these member verses are not separable sayings, since 6:13 cannot stand as a saying at all, and the row's own rationale describes the span as one cumulative portrait resolved by a causal clause. The collection's ruled precedent types a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning verses as one proverb-unit regardless of verse count, which is the byte situation here. The span itself is not in question: the causal opener at 6:15 ties the apodosis back to 6:12, a petuchah closes oshb:Prov.6.15 in WLC (tier-3, single-witness, inventory-confirmed), and 6:16 opens the numerical formula.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.6.12-Prov.6.15 unchanged: retype unit_type and literature_type_guess from proverb_cluster to single_proverb under the ruled continuous-sentence precedent (one syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one proverb-unit regardless of verse count), and re-open the dependent fields a driver swap re-opens - strongest_rejected_alternative, which must then reject the cluster reading on the dependency bytes of 6:13 rather than on the count of verses, plus confidence, observed_substrate_signals and the device_notes deviation sentence. If the adjudicator instead holds that the three participial clauses of 6:13 are separately quotable sayings, proverb_cluster stands and only the rejection sentence needs its byte ground restated; either way this is a type repair, not a span change.

findings.claim: The row's back seam carries a root-level lexical tie that the adjoining row discloses and this row does not, although this row does disclose the adjoining parashah mark at the same seam.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the seam, byte tier, spliced: the preceding row's closing verse reads וּבָֽא כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵאשֶׁ֑ךָ and this row's opening verse continues אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן , ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה . The tie is the halak root across two attested spellings - the skeleton form כמהלך stands in 1 verse book-wide (Prov.6.11) and the skeleton form הולך in 12 verses book-wide (Prov.4.18, Prov.6.12, Prov.7.22, Prov.10.9, Prov.11.13, Prov.13.20, Prov.14.2, Prov.19.1, Prov.20.19, Prov.28.6, Prov.28.18, Prov.28.26; verse counts, skeleton tier) - so neither contiguous sweep alone can see the tie, the allography hazard live at this seam. The adjoining row discloses this recurrence at the same seam; this row discloses only the adjoining petuchah at oshb:Prov.6.11 (tier-3, single-witness, inventory-confirmed) and is silent on the lexical tie, so the seam is documented from one side only against the standing symmetry rule. Which ruled object decides the seam: the address-mode shift, second-person imperative and interrogative material before the seam against the third-person nominal-plus-participial portrait opening at 6:12, with the petuchah as tier-3 corroboration only; the seam holds, the disclosure does not.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span unchanged: add the halak cross-seam disclosure to device_notes naming both attested spellings with their own digits and units (the pre-seam spelling, 1 verse book-wide, at oshb:Prov.6.11; the post-seam spelling, 12 verses book-wide, at oshb:Prov.6.12, both skeleton tier by verse count), state that the seam still rests on the address-mode shift with the petuchah as tier-3 single-witness corroboration, and mirror the adjoining row's wording so the seam is documented from both sides.

findings.claim: The pair is called a short envelope though the repeated noun stands inside each verse's A-colon rather than framing the pair, so no inclusio configuration exists in the bytes.
findings.grounds: Byte tier, spliced: 10:16 reads פְּעֻלַּ֣ת צַדִּ֣יק לְחַיִּ֑ים with the shared prefixed noun standing under the verse's atnach (U+0591, word 3 of 6) and so colon-final in the A-colon, while 10:17 reads אֹ֣רַח לְ֭חַיִּים with the same noun as word 2 of 7, inside its A-colon, that verse's atnach falling one word later on the discipline noun. An envelope or inclusio would require the repetition at the pair's outer edges; the pair's outer edges are instead 10:16's opening word and 10:17's closing run תּוֹכַ֣חַת מַתְעֶֽה , neither of which carries the noun. The cohesion object itself is confirmed exactly as the row states: skeleton לחיים stands in 4 verses book-wide (Prov.10.16, Prov.10.17, Prov.11.19, Prov.19.23; verse counts, contiguous skeleton sweep), and Prov.10.16-Prov.10.17 is the only adjacent pair among them, so the finding is the device name, not the evidence.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.10.16-Prov.10.17 unchanged: replace the envelope wording in boundary_rationale with the byte-accurate configuration, a repeated prefixed noun standing colon-final at oshb:Prov.10.16 and second-word at oshb:Prov.10.17, and leave the verified 4-verse book-wide sweep with its only-adjacent-pair exclusivity as the row's stated cohesion object; the medium confidence is proportionate to that digit and needs no change.

findings.claim: The atomization rival is answered in a weakened form, as a reading of the two verses as unrelated, which the collection's ruled default never requires.
findings.grounds: The collection's ruled default is a single_proverb row per saying, and that default is indifferent to whether adjacent sayings are topically related; rejecting the rival as a reading of the two verses as unrelated therefore answers a weaker rival than the ruled one, which would concede the relation and still ask for two rows. The byte ground the row names does survive re-derivation: skeleton לחיים at 4 verses book-wide (Prov.10.16, Prov.10.17, Prov.11.19, Prov.19.23; verse counts), only adjacent pair. Both edges were re-checked at skeleton tier and are clean, which is why no span change follows: the preceding verse closes מְחִתַּ֖ת דַּלִּ֣ים רֵישָֽׁם and the following verse opens מְכַסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה , and neither shares a content token with the pair at skeleton tier.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span unchanged: restate strongest_rejected_alternative so the rival is the ruled atomization (two single_proverb rows for two adjacent and topically related sayings, the collection's default) and reject it on the rarity digit alone (the shared prefixed noun at 4 verses book-wide by verse count, the only adjacent pair among them), keeping the one-sentence form the collection's rejection rule allows.

findings.claim: An undisclosed catchword of exactly the class this row uses for cohesion straddles its forward edge, while the row argues that edge as the close of the chapter's run, a tier-4 object.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the forward seam, byte tier, spliced: this row's closing verse reads שִׂפְתֵ֣י צַ֭דִּיק יֵדְע֣וּן רָצ֑וֹן , וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת and the following row's opening verse reads מֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭רְמָה תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶ֖בֶן שְׁלֵמָ֣ה רְצוֹנֽוֹ . The straddling object is the favour noun, whose final-nun skeleton spelling is רצון , standing colon-final at 10:32 under that verse's atnach (U+0591, word 4 of 7), and whose medial-nun pre-suffix skeleton spelling is רצונו , standing in the closing word of 11:1. Swept per attested spelling as the toolkit's allography rule requires: the final-nun spelling stands in 8 verses book-wide (Prov.8.35, Prov.10.32, Prov.11.27, Prov.12.2, Prov.14.9, Prov.14.35, Prov.16.13, Prov.18.22) and the medial-nun spelling in 6 (Prov.11.1, Prov.11.20, Prov.12.22, Prov.15.8, Prov.16.15, Prov.19.12), 14 disjoint verses combined at skeleton tier by verse count, and Prov.10.32 with Prov.11.1 is the only adjacent pair among all 14. That is the very argument form this row builds its own cluster on: the row's primary object, skeleton תהפכות , re-swept and confirmed at 9 verses book-wide (Prov.2.12, Prov.2.14, Prov.6.14, Prov.8.13, Prov.10.31, Prov.10.32, Prov.16.28, Prov.16.30, Prov.23.33; verse counts) with Prov.10.31-Prov.10.32 the only adjacent pair. Which ruled object decides this edge: not the chapter division, which is tier-4 metadata and can never carry a seam, and which the row leans on when it argues the pair as closing the chapter's run; what does hold the edge is that both of the row's cohesion objects are absent from 11:1, whose own opener is a commerce-scale construct and whose evaluating frame is the abomination and delight formula pair. No merge is proposed, because 11:1's cohesion objects are disjoint from the pair's; the defect is that a same-class catchword straddles the edge undisclosed on both sides while a tier-4 object is named in its place.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.10.31-Prov.10.32 unchanged: disclose the cross-seam recurrence of the favour noun at the oshb:Prov.10.32 to oshb:Prov.11.1 edge in device_notes with its per-spelling digits and units (final-nun spelling 8 verses book-wide, medial-nun pre-suffix spelling 6 verses, 14 disjoint verses combined at skeleton tier by verse count, the two sites the only adjacent pair among them), state the byte ground that holds the edge notwithstanding, namely that both cohesion objects of this row are absent from Prov.11.1, and drop the chapter-close clause from boundary_rationale as tier-4 texture rather than boundary evidence.

findings.claim: The rejection sentence describes the shared noun as closing both verses, contradicting the row's own rationale, which places it construct-medial in the first member.
findings.grounds: Byte tier, spliced: 10:31 reads פִּֽי צַ֭דִּיק יָנ֣וּב חָכְמָ֑ה וּלְשׁ֥וֹן תַּ֝הְפֻּכ֗וֹת תִּכָּרֵֽת , where the shared noun is word 6 of 7 and the verse's closing word is the finite verb that governs it, exactly as the boundary_rationale states; only 10:32 closes on the noun, וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת . The rejection sentence nonetheless calls the object their shared closing noun, which is true of one member and false of the other by the row's own byte account - an internal inconsistency in the object's description, not in the object itself (skeleton תהפכות , 9 verses book-wide, verse counts, re-swept and confirmed).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span unchanged: restate the object in strongest_rejected_alternative as the shared noun standing verse-final at oshb:Prov.10.32 and construct-medial, word 6 of 7, at oshb:Prov.10.31, matching the boundary_rationale's own byte statement and the 9-verse book-wide sweep.

findings.claim: The rejection's second ground, that the preceding verse carries no part of the virtue-guides and vice-destroys template, is byte-false, and the tie it denies straddles the row's back seam undisclosed.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the back seam, byte tier, spliced: the preceding row's closing verse ends וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה תַּצִּ֥יל מִמָּֽוֶת and this row's opening verse reads צִדְקַ֣ת תָּ֭מִים תְּיַשֵּׁ֣ר דַּרְכּ֑וֹ , with the row's second member opening צִדְקַ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים תַּצִּילֵ֑ם . The rejection says neither neighbour carries the construct opener or the virtue-guides and vice-destroys template; the first half is byte-true, the second is byte-false. 11:4's B-colon pairs a virtue noun of the same root, the absolute spelling וצדקה , with the deliverance verb whose skeleton spelling is תציל , standing in 5 verses book-wide (Prov.10.2, Prov.11.4, Prov.11.6, Prov.19.19, Prov.23.14; verse counts, skeleton tier) - Prov.11.4 and Prov.11.6 are two of those five, the second realised with an object suffix - so 11:4 carries precisely the virtue-delivers half of the template the rejection denies it, one verse outside the row's own edge and undisclosed under the cross-seam cohesion rule. Which ruled object decides the edge and keeps it standing: the exclusive construct spelling, skeleton צדקת , re-swept and confirmed at 2 verses book-wide (Prov.11.5, Prov.11.6; verse counts) and verse-initial in both, against 11:4, which opens instead with a negated verb clause, לֹא יוֹעִ֣יל ה֭וֹן , and carries the absolute noun rather than that construct. The edge therefore holds on the construct-opener object alone and no span change follows; the rejection's second ground must be withdrawn or restated.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.11.5-Prov.11.6 unchanged: withdraw the clause denying the template to Prov.11.4 and replace it with the byte-true ground (Prov.11.4 opens with a negated verb clause and carries the absolute virtue noun, not the verse-initial construct spelling whose sweep digit is 2 verses book-wide), and add a cross-seam disclosure naming the shared deliverance verb at Prov.11.4 and Prov.11.6 with its digit and unit (skeleton spelling, 5 verses book-wide, verse counts). The high confidence remains supported by the 2-verse exclusive construct opener and needs no change; no merge into Prov.11.4 is proposed, since that verse lacks the construct opener the row is built on.

findings.claim: The row's second cohesion object, the shared giving-and-withholding-and-reward pattern, is byte-present in the preceding verse too, so it does not stop at the row's back edge and cannot serve as cohesion evidence.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the back seam, byte tier, spliced: the preceding row's closing verse reads in full יֵ֣שׁ מְ֭פַזֵּר וְנוֹסָ֥ף ע֑וֹד וְחוֹשֵׂ֥ךְ מִ֝יֹּ֗שֶׁר אַךְ לְמַחְסֽוֹר - an existential pair whose A-colon, to the atnach (U+0591, word 4 of 8), states giving that increases and whose B-colon states withholding that ends in want, WEB “There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.” (web:Prov.11.24) - and this row's opening verse reads נֶֽפֶשׁ בְּרָכָ֥ה תְדֻשָּׁ֑ן , opening the giving-and-reward half of that same pattern, with the second member carrying the withholding half, מֹ֣נֵֽעַ בָּ֭ר , against וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר . The row offers that pattern as evidence beyond the shared token, stating that the two verses argue it and not merely a shared abstract theme; but the pattern is equally present one verse outside the span, so it cannot distinguish the row's own edge, and under the collection's ruled bar a shared pattern that does not stop at the seam is theme-level glue rather than cohesion evidence. Which ruled object decides the edge and keeps it standing: the shared noun alone, re-swept and confirmed exactly as the row states - skeleton ברכה in 3 verses book-wide (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26; verse counts), Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 the only adjacent pair, with the distinct construct spelling ברכת separately confirmed at 3 verses (Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25) and rightly excluded from that figure. The forward edge is clean at skeleton tier: the following verse opens שֹׁ֣חֵֽר ט֭וֹב and shares no content token with the pair. No span change follows, because extending into Prov.11.24 would rest on the theme alone, which the collection's bar forbids.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 unchanged: demote the giving-and-withholding-and-reward pattern from cohesion evidence to disclosed texture that continues into Prov.11.24, in both boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals, leaving the shared noun sweep (3 verses book-wide, the only adjacent pair among them) as the row's sole stated cluster object; the existing medium_low confidence and the frontier flag remain proportionate to that thinner stated evidence and need no change.

findings.claim: The signals field's adjacency statement names the wrong two sites as listed, since the series is given out of book order.
findings.grounds: The signals field lists the three sweep hits in the order Prov.11.25 (bare form), then Prov.10.7 and Prov.11.26 (prefixed forms), and then states that the latter two of these three sites sit adjacent. As listed, the latter two are Prov.10.7 and Prov.11.26, which are not adjacent; the adjacent pair is Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26, as the boundary_rationale states correctly and as the re-sweep confirms (skeleton ברכה , 3 verses book-wide, verse counts, hits at Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25 and Prov.11.26). The standing ordinal rule requires the series to byte-settle before an ordinal is asserted over it, so the statement is defective as written even though its underlying set and digit are exact.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span unchanged: re-order the three sweep hits in book order (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26) or name the adjacent pair explicitly as Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26, so the ordinal statement matches the swept series; the digit and the set stay as shipped.

findings.claim: The rationale's leading cohesion statement, that both verses close on the tongue-noun, is byte-false for both verses, and the device_notes restatement of the position is byte-false for the first member.
findings.grounds: Byte tier, both verses spliced in full: 12:18 reads יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְר֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא - 7 words, closing on its healing noun, with the tongue-noun as word 5, the first word of the B-colon that follows the atnach (U+0591, word 4 of 7), that is, third from the verse's end - and 12:19 reads שְֽׂפַת אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר - 8 words, closing on its falsehood noun, with the tongue-noun as word 7, second-to-last in the verse and second-to-last in its own B-colon (atnach at word 4 of 8). So the rationale's leading statement, that both verses close on the noun, is byte-false for both verses, and the device_notes correction, that the noun sits as the second-to-last word of its own colon in both verses, is byte-false for 12:18, where it is colon-initial: וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא against לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר . The staged universals checker independently raises that device_notes clause as a positional universal carried without a digit-bearing sweep. The shared object itself is real and unaffected, so this is a warrant-statement defect, not a boundary defect.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 unchanged: delete the close-on wording from boundary_rationale and the second-to-last-word-of-its-own-colon-in-both-verses clause from device_notes, and restate the object as a shared noun standing in the B-colon of both verses, colon-initial at oshb:Prov.12.18 (word 5 of 7, immediately after the atnach) and second-to-last at oshb:Prov.12.19 (word 7 of 8), so the positional claim matches the bytes and no longer carries an undigited positional universal.

findings.claim: This row and the adjoining row give incompatible accounts of the same back seam, since this row discloses a falsehood-root recurrence that the adjoining row denies outright.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the back seam, byte tier, spliced: the preceding row's closing verse ends וְעֵ֖ד שְׁקָרִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה and this row's opening verse begins יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה . The object at issue is the falsehood noun, skeleton שקר , re-swept at 20 verses book-wide (Prov.6.17, Prov.6.19, Prov.10.18, Prov.11.18, Prov.12.17, Prov.12.19, Prov.12.22, Prov.13.5, Prov.14.5, Prov.17.4, Prov.17.7, Prov.19.5, Prov.19.9, Prov.20.17, Prov.21.6, Prov.25.14, Prov.25.18, Prov.26.28, Prov.29.12, Prov.31.30; verse counts, skeleton tier), standing at Prov.12.17 and at this row's own Prov.12.19, לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר , but not at Prov.12.18 - the tie therefore skips the seam verse. This row discloses that recurrence and holds its boundary; the adjoining row states that its verse shares no lexeme with either member of this span, which is byte-false for Prov.12.19. Which ruled object decides the seam itself: at the immediate junction Prov.12.17 and Prov.12.18 share no content token at skeleton tier, so the atomic boundary holds on the bytes and no span change follows - but the corpus carries two contradictory statements about one object at one seam and only one of them can stand, which is a cross-row coherence finding rather than a defect in this row's own account.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to the seam pair as one edit, spans unchanged: keep this row's disclosure, which is the byte-true account, and correct the adjoining row's no-shared-lexeme sentence to name the recurrence of the falsehood noun at oshb:Prov.12.17 and oshb:Prov.12.19 with its digit and unit (skeleton spelling, 20 verses book-wide, verse counts) while stating that the immediate junction Prov.12.17 to Prov.12.18 shares no content token at skeleton tier, so both sides of the seam carry the same object description.

findings.claim: The row's only cohesion object carries no book-wide digit, though the digit and the pair's exclusivity are both material and both available.
findings.grounds: The row's entire warrant is one repeated content token, and no book-wide digit is given for it anywhere in the row. Re-swept: skeleton לשון stands in 16 verses book-wide (Prov.6.17, Prov.6.24, Prov.10.20, Prov.10.31, Prov.12.18, Prov.12.19, Prov.15.2, Prov.15.4, Prov.16.1, Prov.17.4, Prov.18.21, Prov.21.6, Prov.25.15, Prov.25.23, Prov.26.28, Prov.28.23; verse counts, skeleton tier) - a common noun in a speech-saturated collection - of which Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 is nonetheless the only adjacent pair. Both figures are material to a cluster resting on that one token, and every comparable cluster row in this slice supplies its own digit. The row's medium_low confidence, its frontier flag and its explicit thinness disclosure remain proportionate once the digits are supplied, and the registered thin-catchword class is the ruled disposition for a row of this kind, so no retirement is proposed.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span and confidence unchanged: add the digit-bearing sweep to boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals, naming the swept object and unit - the exact skeleton spelling of the tongue-noun, 16 verses book-wide by verse count, with Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 the only adjacent pair among them - so the thin-catchword warrant is stated with the figure it depends on.

findings.claim: The rationale quotes a Hebrew form from a ketiv/qere verse without carrying the K/Q disclosure in that same field.
findings.grounds: The boundary_rationale splices a pointed form from oshb:Prov.13.20, a verse the inventory records with 2 ketiv/qere notes (WLC, single witness), and the staged verse bytes carry both unpointed ketiv tokens inline before their pointed qere, הלוך הוֹלֵ֣ךְ and וחכם יֶחְכָּ֑ם , so any quotation from this verse crosses a K/Q site. The disclosure exists and is exact in device_notes (2 notes, both pairs named as the inventory has them, single-witness), but it is absent from the field that carries the quotation; the staged citation sweep raises exactly this as its single warn on this row, and the standing rule places the K/Q disclosure in the field whose quoted span touches it. Byte tier throughout; the row's own cohesion object, the plural fools-noun, is unaffected.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.13.19-Prov.13.20 unchanged: carry a short ketiv/qere disclosure into boundary_rationale beside the quoted form (2 notes at oshb:Prov.13.20, WLC single witness, the pointed qere quoted), or move the quotation into the field that already discloses it; the device_notes disclosure itself is exact against the inventory and needs no change.

findings.claim: The row's forward edge carries a consonantal recurrence that the adjoining row discloses and adjudicates while this row is silent, and the same consonantal set already stands inside this row's own span undisclosed on both sides.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the forward seam, byte tier, spliced: this row's closing verse ends וְרֹעֶ֖ה כְסִילִ֣ים יֵרֽוֹעַ and the following row's opening verse begins חַ֭טָּאִים תְּרַדֵּ֣ף רָעָ֑ה ; the same consonantal set already stands inside this row's own span, at the close of 13:19, ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע . The adjoining row discloses the pair at the seam and rules it a homograph rather than a catchword; this row is silent on it, and neither row discloses the site inside 13:19. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so that lexeme-identity ruling cannot be machine-verified here and rests on the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings - WEB has “suffers harm” (web:Prov.13.20) against “Misfortune pursues sinners” (web:Prov.13.21) - so it is recorded here, not adjudicated. Which ruled object decides the edge: the row's own cohesion object, the exact plural fools-noun whose 17 book-wide sites are listed in this row's other finding, is absent from Prov.13.21, so the edge holds and no span change follows; the defect is that a seam object is documented from one side only, against the standing symmetry rule.
